subject: Biology
topic_title: Structural/functional and behavioural adaptations of organisms
content: a. Adaptive colouration and its functions; b. Behavioural adaptations in social animals; c. Structural adaptations in organisms
objectives: Candidates should be able to: i. describe how structures, functions and behaviour adapt organisms to their environment and way of life. ii. categorize countershading in fish, toads, snakes and warning colouration in mushrooms. iii. differentiate castes in social insects like termites and their functions in the colony/hive. iv. account for basking in lizards, territorial behaviour under unfavourable conditions (hibernation and aestivation), obtaining food (beaks/legs of birds, mouthparts of insects), protection and defence (stick insects, praying mantis, toad), securing mates (display in Agama lizards, birds), regulating body temperature (skin, feathers, hairs), conserving water (spines in plants, scales in mammals).

subject: Biology
content: a. Modes of nutrition: i. Autotrophic ii. Heterotrophic. b. Types of nutrition. c. Plant nutrition: i. Photosynthesis ii. Chemosynthesis iii. objectives: Candidates should be able to: i. compare autotrophic and heterotrophic modes of nutrition. ii. provide examples from both flowering and non-flowering plants. iii. compare photosynthetic and chemosynthetic modes of nutrition. iv. differentiate examples of heterotrophic feeding: holozoic (sheep and man), parasitic (roundworm, tapeworm, Loranthus), saprophytic (Rhizopus, mushroom), carnivorous plants (sundew, bladderwort) and determine their nutritional value. v. differentiate light and dark reactions of photosynthesis. vi. determine the necessity of light, carbon (IV) oxide and chlorophyll in photosynthesis. vii. detect the presence of starch in a leaf as evidence of photosynthesis. viii. identify macro- and micro-elements required by plants. ix. recognise deficiency symptoms of nitrogen, phosphorous and potassium. x. indicate sources of the various classes of food. xi. determine nutritional value of food. xii. relate importance and deficiency (e.g. scurvy, rickets, kwashiorkor) of each food class. xiii. determine the importance of a balanced diet. xiv. detect the presence of a food type from the result of a given experiment. xv. describe the structure of a typical mammalian tooth. xvi. differentiate types of mammalian tooth and relate structure to function. xvii. compare dental formulae of man, sheep and dog. xviii. relate structure of components of the alimentary canal and accessory organs (liver, pancreas, gall bladder) to their functions. xix. identify general characteristics of digestive enzymes. xx. associate enzymes with digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats. xxi. determine the end products of these classes of food.

subject: Biology
content: a. Respiratory organs and surfaces. b. Mechanism of gaseous exchange in: i. Plants ii. Animals. c. Aerobic respiration. d. Anaerobic respiration.
objectives: Candidates should be able to: i. explain significance of respiration. ii. describe a simplified outline of chemical processes in glycolysis and Krebs cycle with reference to ATP production. iii. deduce gaseous exchange, products, and heat energy production during respiration from an experimental set up. iv. describe respiratory organs/surfaces and the organisms in which they occur: body surface, gill, trachea, lungs, stomata, lenticel. v. describe the mechanism for opening/closing of the stomata. vi. determine respiratory mechanisms in plants and animals. vii. examine the role of oxygen in liberation of energy for living activities. viii. explain effect of insufficient oxygen supply to muscles. ix. use yeast cells and sugar solution to demonstrate fermentation. x. state economic importance of yeasts.
